comments.body:
EVIDENCE for 'Each deletion is a separate commit so either can be reverted independently'.

The two deletions landed on origin/main as two distinct commits, pushed as two distinct Gerrit changes (a relation chain), so either can be reverted on its own:

  6d8ea3143a  Delete dead bug_close_reason_ok predicate      (Gerrit change 1475)
  c89a2ddcc4  Delete the dead reconciler _attestation module (Gerrit change 1476)

Command and output:
  $ git log origin/main --oneline --grep=723f -5
  c89a2ddcc4 Delete the dead reconciler _attestation module
  6d8ea3143a Delete dead bug_close_reason_ok predicate

Both carry the rebar-ticket: 723f-c5b2-d83b-43cb trailer and a DCO sign-off, and both are Verified +1 / LLM-Review +1 and MERGED. The criterion is met on main; it is not visible from a worktree HEAD that predates the merge, which is why the verifier could not see it.

compiled_state.description:
Two units have zero production references, confirmed symbol-by-symbol including the reconciler's
dynamic `_load()`-by-filename seam, and independently re-verified by a blue-team pass.

**`bug_close_reason_ok`** (`_commands/txn.py:154-160`) — zero callers repo-wide. Its docstring
actively lies: "Shared by `transition_core`'s close guard and the completion gate's pre-check... so
the two cannot drift." Both consumers migrated to `bug_close_class_ok` (`txn.py:262`,
`close_precheck.py:183`), whose sibling docstring makes the identical claim truthfully. A reader
auditing the close guard finds two near-identical "shared anti-drift guard" functions and can pick
the dead one, reintroducing free-text validation into a path that enforces a bounded enum.

**`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_attestation.py`** — the WHOLE module (126 LOC, three symbols:
`verify_manifest_hash:16`, `build_acli_client_from_env:41`, `verify_attested_commit:72`), kept alive
only by its own ~200-line unit test and carried through unrelated refactors. A GPG-signature-verifying
gate that is tested, maintained, and never invoked is a false assurance signal.
`adapters/jira/backend.py:192` still claims the adapter "Preserves the pre-97f2
`build_acli_client_from_env` contract", implying a live partner that does not exist.

Flagged in the 2026-07-07 audit and unremediated since.

CASCADE: consider caller + dynamic-reference (reflection / string dispatch / DI / dynamic import)
impact. The reconciler's dynamic loader was already cleared during verification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `bug_close_reason_ok` is deleted; `bug_close_class_ok`'s docstring is the only anti-drift claim
- [x] `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_attestation.py` and its unit test are deleted
- [x] The dangling contract claim at `adapters/jira/backend.py:192` is corrected
- [x] Each deletion is a separate commit so either can be reverted independently [operator-attested]

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E4/G1G2/G6) — the consumer set was wrong

The paragraph above said `_attestation.py` is "kept alive only by its own ~200-line unit
test". That is FALSE, and verified so against the tree. There are THREE consumers, and a
deletion that removes only the unit test leaves a broken suite:

1. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_attestation.py` — the known unit test. It loads the
   module BY PATH (`ATTESTATION_PATH = .../rebar_reconciler/_attestation.py`, `:27`) via
   `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` (`:31`).
2. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config_jira_wiring.py:217,226,233` — a config-routing
   test for ticket 0ac6. It does `from rebar_reconciler import _attestation` and calls
   `_attestation.build_acli_client_from_env()`. This is an UNENUMERATED consumer with nothing to
   do with attestation testing; deleting the module breaks it.
3. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py:42,147` — two parametrized guard
   tuples (`_NO_INLINE_ACLICLIENT`, `_ZERO_ADAPTER_IMPORT_SCALAR_CORE`) list the string
   `"_attestation.py"` and `read_text()` each path. Deleting the file makes those cases raise
   `FileNotFoundError` rather than pass.

Consumers 2 and 3 are exactly the class the repo's own navigation guidance warns about: a
symbol/file named AS A STRING, which semantic search does not surface. The original CASCADE note
cleared the reconciler's dynamic `_load()` seam but did not grep for the filename as a string.

This does not overturn the deletion — no PRODUCTION module imports `_attestation`, so the
"tested, maintained, never invoked" finding stands. It changes the MECHANISM.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above for the `_attestation` half)

- [x] `bug_close_reason_ok` is deleted; `bug_close_class_ok`'s docstring is the only anti-drift claim
- [x] `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_attestation.py` is deleted, together with ALL THREE consumers
      handled: its unit test deleted; `test_config_jira_wiring.py`'s use of
      `build_acli_client_from_env` re-pointed or removed with its intent (0ac6 config routing)
      preserved by another assertion; and `"_attestation.py"` removed from BOTH guard tuples in
      `test_backend_neutrality.py`
- [x] `grep -rn '_attestation' tests/ src/` returns no live reference after the change
- [x] The dangling contract claim at `adapters/jira/backend.py:192` is corrected
- [x] Each deletion is a separate commit so either can be reverted independently [operator-attested]


## CORRECTION 2 (plan-review BLOCK round 3, criteria G1G2/G6) — SYMBOL refs, not just filename

Correction 1's AC greps for `_attestation`. That is insufficient: three further references name
the SYMBOL `build_acli_client_from_env` rather than the module filename, so the grep misses them.
Full verified reference set (5 sites):

| site | kind | after deletion |
|---|---|---|
| `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:44` | prose in `BackendEnvError`'s docstring, "at existing call sites (e.g. ``build_acli_client_from_env``) is preserved" | dangling symbol |
| `adapters/jira/backend.py:192` | prose, "Preserves the pre-97f2 ``build_acli_client_from_env`` contract" | reads as a LIVE partner |
| `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py:10` | module docstring, "via the ``_load_acli`` / ``build_acli_client_from_env`` seams" | dangling symbol |
| `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config_jira_wiring.py:226,233` | live CALLS | broken test |
| `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_attestation.py` | the unit test | deleted with the module |

### The re-point target, named (Correction 1 left this open)

`test_config_jira_wiring.py:216-233` asserts the 0ac6 routing end-to-end: url/user resolved from
`rebar.toml`, token from env, `project_default` applying `DIG`, and a `RuntimeError` naming
`JIRA_API_TOKEN` when the token is absent.

The live equivalent is **`JiraBackend.assert_env_ready()`**
(`adapters/jira/backend.py:189`), which is the SAME contract by construction: it calls
`acli_subprocess.resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG")` and raises `BackendEnvError`
(a `RuntimeError` subclass) naming the missing var(s). Its own docstring already says it
"Preserves the pre-97f2 ``build_acli_client_from_env`` contract".

So the re-point is: assert the fail-fast through `assert_env_ready()`, and the `DIG`
project_default through `resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG")` (or `backend.query_project`
for the no-default read path). No assertion is lost.

## Acceptance Criteria (FINAL — supersedes all lists above)

- [x] `bug_close_reason_ok` is deleted; `bug_close_class_ok`'s docstring is the only anti-drift claim
- [x] `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_attestation.py` and `tests/.../state/test_attestation.py` are deleted
- [x] `test_config_jira_wiring.py`'s two calls are re-pointed to `JiraBackend.assert_env_ready()` +
      `resolve_jira_settings(project_default="DIG")`, preserving BOTH 0ac6 assertions (the `DIG`
      default and the `RuntimeError` naming `JIRA_API_TOKEN`)
- [x] `"_attestation.py"` is removed from BOTH guard tuples in `test_backend_neutrality.py`
      (`_NO_INLINE_ACLICLIENT`, `_ZERO_ADAPTER_IMPORT_SCALAR_CORE`), which `read_text()` the path
- [x] The three prose references are corrected so none names a nonexistent symbol as a live
      partner: `_backend.py:44`, `adapters/jira/backend.py:192`, `test_backend_neutrality.py:10`
      (the pre-97f2 contract may be cited as HISTORY, but not as a call site that exists)
- [x] BOTH greps are clean afterwards: `grep -rn '_attestation' src/ tests/` AND
      `grep -rn 'build_acli_client_from_env' src/ tests/` return no reference to a deleted symbol
- [x] Each deletion is a separate commit so either can be reverted independently [operator-attested]
